newsitem.title: BURMA: Former Burma military council chief Saw Maung dies.
newsitem.headline: Former Burma military council chief Saw Maung dies.

text.p: General Saw Maung, who chaired Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) when it was set up in 1988, died of a heart attack on Thursday at his residence, a government statement said.
Saw Maung, 69, retired from the SLORC in 1991 and was replaced by Senior General Than Shwe.
"The general retired from the chairmanship (of the SLORC) in 1991 due to health reasons,' the brief statement added.
The SLORC took power in September 1988 after months of pro-democracy demonstrations.
Saw Maung was a protege of former Burma military strongman and ex-president General Ne Win, who is still alive.
Ne Win stepped down from government and politics after more than a quarter century in power in 1988.
